claims.text: Cold rolling followed by tailored annealing will refine the microstructure of MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials.
The proposed thermomechanical processing will improve mechanical performance while retaining the large magnetocaloric effect of the as-cast state.
As-cast MnNiSi-based alloys have relatively coarse grains.
The coarse-grained as-cast material exhibits high magnetic entropy change but limited mechanical robustness.
Room-temperature cold rolling introduces plastic deformation and promotes grain refinement.
A suitably chosen annealing treatment will promote controlled recrystallization without excessive grain coarsening or alteration of the magnetostructural phase.
Cold rolling and annealing will produce a refined and homogenized grain structure with increased grain-boundary density.
Increased grain-boundary density will increase strength by inhibiting dislocation motion.
The processed microstructure will maintain the magnetostructural transition responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
Grain refinement increases strength through the Hall–Petch effect.
Grain refinement from deformation processing increases ductility via the Hall–Petch effect.
Annealing restores ductility by relieving excessive work hardening without causing detrimental phase transformations.
Controlled microstructural evolution preserves the structural–magnetic coupling that produces a large magnetic entropy change.
The processed material will have higher tensile strength than the as-cast control.
The processed material will have greater ductility than the as-cast control.
Under identical magnetic-field changes, the processed material will retain a magnetic entropy-change magnitude similar to that of the as-cast control.
Overly aggressive annealing may compromise magnetocaloric performance by excessive microstructural smoothing or unwanted phase transformations.
Analogous thermomechanical strategies have improved mechanical properties in similar multifunctional alloys.
